A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MixKV research work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-understanding, GUI-grounding, and LongBench evaluations, component ablations, redundancy analyses, and inference-efficiency measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds controlled redundancy measurements, HeadKV/LooGLE comparisons, and evaluations on larger and MoE models.

M1.justification: Importance scoring, key-diversity scoring, head-wise adaptive mixing, and cache selection remain unchanged, as does Algorithm 1. The added main-text Equation (5) restates the mixing formula already present in v1's appendix; the HeadKV experiments document no procedural adaptation.

E1.justification: Table 5 adds LooGLE long-dependency tasks covering document QA, information retrieval, timelines, and computation. The existing image benchmarks, ScreenSpot-v2, and LongBench remain. Larger and MoE model evaluations use retained image-task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds evaluated HeadKV versus HeadKV+MixKV comparisons in Table 5. It also adds Full KV reference rows to the image-understanding comparison in Table 1, where they were absent in v1. Existing compression comparators are retained.

E3.justification: New experiments substantially extend model configurations to InternVL3-38B and Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B-Instruct at budgets 128 and 64. HeadKV is evaluated at budgets 1024 and 128. Figure 5 adds a controlled model/input comparison averaging 100 samples from each of LongBench and TextVQA; retained experiments keep their stated settings.

E4.justification: Appendix A.2 and Figure 5 add a targeted control testing Qwen2 and Qwen2-VL on text, alongside Qwen2-VL on vision-language inputs, to probe architecture versus input-type explanations for redundancy. Existing component ablations, efficiency analyses, and semantic-coverage visualizations are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. New results retain point estimates and baseline differences. Figure 5's 100-example averaging specifies analysis sample size rather than a new uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Tables 5–7, Figure 5, and Table 1's Full KV rows substantially expand reported outcomes; matched original scores remain unchanged. New MoE OCRBench results at budget 64 are 55.2 for SnapKV and 68.8 with MixKV. HeadKV's LooGLE average improves from 8.44 to 8.69 at budget 128, but declines from 9.21 to 9.16 at 1024.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and redundancy derivation remain unchanged. Equation (5) newly displays in the main text the weighted score already specified in v1's Algorithm 1. No new assumptions, proofs, or substantive mathematical reasoning are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about semantic redundancy, adaptive importance/diversity mixing, compatibility, and efficiency. The abstract's numerical improvement claims also remain unchanged; additional experiments support the existing contribution.

C2.justification: Appendix A.2 newly interprets similar text-only redundancy patterns as evidence that architecture alone does not explain the observed gap. Appendix A.4 discusses larger-model and MoE applicability. Earlier task-dependent caveats remain, but the retained 8B-only limitation now contradicts the expanded experiments.

D1.justification: The implementation description, observation-window specification, normalization procedures, Algorithm 1, and code-access information are retained. Added experimental configurations are not accompanied by new implementation instructions, hardware specifications, or software-environment details.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially broadens positioning through a new Long-Context Optimization discussion covering efficient architectures, model compression, and data compression, explicitly placing MixKV in the last category. References expand to sparse/linear attention, state-space models, pruning, quantization, distillation, HeadKV, and newer LVLMs.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section order are retained. Changes include localized rewriting of Section 4.2, expanded related work, two added appendix subsections, explicit main-text presentation of the mixing equation, terminology changes, and the conference header. Appendix A.2 contains an unresolved section reference.

P2.justification: v2 adds a three-panel annotated redundancy heatmap and Tables 5–7, substantially extending the visual presentation of evidence. Table 1 gains Full KV rows and a revised caption. Existing tables are redistributed, while the appendix efficiency and scatter plots retain their content under new numbering.

improvement.justification: Full KV references, the within-model redundancy control, and larger/MoE evaluations improve assessment of compression losses and generality, partially addressing v1's scale limitation. HeadKV and LooGLE also broaden validation. These benefits are tempered by sparse documentation of the added experiments and Appendix A.7's now-incorrect statement that evaluation stops at 8B.
